panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A shows hematoxylin and eosin stain revealing solid proliferation of atypical cells exhibiting features characteristic of rhabdoid tumors, specifically the presence of eccentric round nuclei and globular cytoplasmic structures. B: Panel B shows immunohistochemical staining positive for CD10, supporting the diagnosis of a neoplastic process consistent with rhabdoid tumor. C: Panel C shows negative immunostaining for cytokeratin 7, a finding useful in the characterization of certain kidney neoplasms. D: Panel D shows positive immunohistochemical staining for D3 in neoplastic cells, further supporting the diagnosis of the rhabdoid tumor.
panels.attribution_text: Fiore et al. Consumptive hypothyroidism in a patient with malignant rhabdoid tumor of the kidney: case report on a newly found association.. European thyroid journal 2022. doi:10.1530/etj-22-0006. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological aspects of the renal carcinoma with rhabdoid features. (A) Hematoxylin and eosin stain; the histology shows a solid proliferation of highly atypical cells, a subset of which are of large size, polygonal, with eccentric round nuclei and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm with a paranuclear globular structure, conferring the typical rhabdoid aspect. (B) Intense immunoreactivity for CD10 and (C) lack of immunostaining for cytokeratin 7 are in support of the diagnosis. (D) Immunohistochemical staining for D3 is present in numerous neoplastic cells as granular brown paramembranous cytoplasmic precipitate (hematoxylin and eosin and immunoperoxidase, x200).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: The panel displays hematoxylin and eosin stained tissue showing spindle cell proliferation with a rhabdoid appearance and nuclear atypia, consistent with Rhabdoid Tumor of the Kidney. B: The panel shows immunohistochemical staining demonstrating cytoplasmic positivity for cytokeratin, a diagnostic marker for the tumor. C: The panel shows immunohistochemical staining demonstrating positive expression of vimentin and Cyclin-D1 in the tumor cells.
panels.attribution_text: Lahmar et al. Malignant Rhabdoid Tumor of the Kidney in a Child With Xeroderma Pigmentosum: Incidence or Coincidence?. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.27049. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Histological examination of the tumor shows a diffuse proliferation of spindle cells arranged in diffuse sheets with a rhabdoid appearance, tumor cells shows evident atypia with enlarged, irregular and hyperchromatic nuclei, the cytoplasm is mostly eosinophilic (A). Several mitotic figures were seen. Immunohistochemical staining shows a positivity for cytokeratin (B), vimentin (C), and Cyclin-D1. Tumor cells were negative for WT1, CD34, PS100, Ck7, desmin, CD10 and LCA. LCA: leukocyte-common antigen
in_text_mentions: A lymphadenopathy biopsy was performed. The histopathological examination revealed a tumor proliferation arranged in sheets made of spindle-shaped rhabdoid appearance with the presence of tumor necrosis. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated focal expression of cytokeratin and vimentin by tumor cells (Figure 3) with lacking INI-1 immunohistochemical staining.

in_text_mentions: Initial laboratory investigations revealed leukocytosis. Abdominal ultrasound (US) demonstrated a solid 6 x 5.3 cm mass at the upper pole of the right kidney with thickened renal parenchyma. On performing computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen, a lobulated soft tissue arising from the kidney was seen with areas of necrosis (Figure 1).
